top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient's symptoms and diagnostic results, including the presence of a hypervascular mass on imaging and smooth muscle and vascular channels on histology, are most consistent with Angioleiomyoma.

Although the patient's symptoms and some diagnostic results are consistent with Leiomyoma, the presence of a hypervascular mass on imaging and vascular channels on histology make Angioleiomyoma a more likely diagnosis.

The presence of vascular channels on histology and a mass supplied by a large feeding artery and drained via a solitary large vein into the portal venous system are consistent with Hemangioma, but other diagnostic results are more consistent with Angioleiomyoma.
The patient's symptoms and diagnostic results, including the lack of significant mitotic activity and no evidence of tumor necrosis, are not consistent with Leiomyosarcoma.
The patient's symptoms and diagnostic results, including the lack of CD117-positive on immunohistochemistry, are not consistent with Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST).
